children: Jayatri Nag Kolkata: Reliance Industries will make investments in four to five sectors in West Bengal, with a team from the company set to visit the state next week, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday. "The Ambani family invited me during last week's Ganapati festival.

During a meeting at their residence, Mukesh Ambaniji and Anant Ambaniji assured me that they will invest in 4-5 sectors in Bengal. They will send a team next week," Adhikari said. The state has also accepted the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO's) proposal for a new Missile Launching Station at East Midnapore's Junput, which was not accepted by the previous government, Adhikari said.

On Thursday, Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Karan Adani are expected to do the bhumi pujan of the 'Adani Arogya Mandir', a 2,000-bed hospital in Bengal, according to him. "An era of reform has already started in West Bengal", Adhikari said, adding that the state government has "a positive attitude" towards investments, in contrast to the "dole politics" culture of the previous Trinamool Congress government. "The BJP government will eradicate the negative attitude of the Left Front and 15-year rule of the Trinamool government.

We are directly purchasing land for the state's industrialisation," the chief minister said during an event where the government handed over 33 land parcels to as many industrialists. "The Left Front destroyed industries in Bengal from Chittaranjan in Asansol to Titagarh and Barrackpore. Later, came the Mamata government, which clearly said it will not give land.

Industries cannot be built on air, they need land. The late former chief minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharya tried, but his party's policies were very poor," Adhikari said. "Today, the chief minister is laying the foundation for an Atma Nirbhar and Viksit Bengal by handing over land to 33 industrialists. The government is not even 150 days old.

There is not just political change but tangible change ," industry and commerce minister Tapas Roy said. "We have to transform and reconstruct the state. We can see diverse kinds of investments - from defence equipment, solar cell modules to semiconductors, steel products to jute and jewellery, " Roy said. "Everyone is making a beeline to Kolkata.West Bengal will rise to the position it held in the 1920s or 30s," said chief secretary Manoj Kumar Agarwal.

title: RIL may Invest in 4-5 Sectors in Bengal, Team to Visit State: CM
